articles.heading: Type 1 Recognized vs. Type 2 Nonrecognized Events
articles.text:
• Evaluation Cutoff (ASC 855-10-25): SEC filers evaluate subsequent events through the date financial statements are ISSUED; non-SEC entities evaluate through the date financial statements are AVAILABLE TO BE ISSUED (and must disclose that date).
• Recognized vs. Nonrecognized: Conditions existing at the balance sheet date adjust financial statements; conditions arising after the balance sheet date are disclosed if material.

articles.heading: Key Cross-Framework Differences

articles.heading: Scope & Core Objective (Public Summary)
articles.text: Establishes the control-based derecognition criteria for transfers of financial assets (securitizations, receivable factoring, repurchase agreements) requiring legal isolation, transferee pledge/exchange rights, and absence of effective control.

articles.heading: Control-Based Derecognition (Legal Isolation) & Repos
articles.text:
• Three Sale Criteria (ASC 860-10-40-5): (a) Legal isolation — transferred assets are put presumptively beyond the reach of the transferor even in bankruptcy ('true sale' legal opinion); (b) Transferee right to pledge/exchange; (c) Transferor does not maintain effective control (e.g., repurchase agreement).
• No Continuing Involvement Partial Derecognition: Binary sale vs. secured borrowing outcome for entire financial assets (or qualifying 'participating interests').

articles.heading: Key Cross-Framework Differences
articles.text: • Major Divergence from IFRS 9.3.2 / CAS 23: IFRS 9 focuses primarily on transfer of RISKS AND REWARDS before evaluating control (and permits continuing-involvement partial derecognition); ASC 860 focuses strictly on LEGAL ISOLATION AND CONTROL.

articles.text: Governs accounting for short-duration and long-duration insurance contracts, modernized by ASU 2018-12 (Long-Duration Targeted Improvements — LDTI) requiring annual assumption updates, market risk benefits at fair value, and upper-medium-grade bond discounting.

articles.heading: Short- vs. Long-Duration Insurance & LDTI Modernization
articles.text: • Long-Duration Targeted Improvements (LDTI, ASU 2018-12): Liability for future policy benefits updated annually for cash flow assumptions; discount rate updated quarterly via OCI using upper-medium-grade fixed-income instrument yields; Market Risk Benefits (MRBs) measured at fair value; DAC amortized on a constant-level basis.

articles.heading: Key Cross-Framework Differences
articles.text: • Major Divergence from IFRS 17 / CAS 25: IFRS 17 builds a unified current-value Contractual Service Margin (CSM) model across all insurance contracts; US GAAP (ASC 944 + LDTI) retains separate short-duration vs. long-duration models without a CSM.

articles.text: Establishes capitalization of costs incurred to develop computer software to be sold, leased, or otherwise marketed (ASC 985-20) once 'technological feasibility' is established through general release.

articles.heading: Technological Feasibility Window & Amortization
articles.text:
• Capitalization Window (ASC 985-20-25): Expense all costs as R&D (ASC 730) until 'technological feasibility' (detailed program design or working model) is established; capitalize coding/testing costs until product is available for general release to customers.
• Amortization & NRV Test (ASC 985-20-35): Amortize at the greater of revenue-ratio method or straight-line; evaluate unamortized cost against Net Realizable Value each balance sheet date.

articles.heading: Key Cross-Framework Differences
articles.text: • Under US GAAP, software development has two distinct models (ASC 985-20 for external sale vs. ASC 350-40 for internal-use/SaaS); under IFRS, both sit under IAS 38's unified 6-criteria development model.

articles.heading: Top US GAAP vs. IFRS Divergence Map (Reference Only)
articles.text:
• High-Impact Divergence Areas Covered:
  – Revenue (ASC 606 vs. IFRS 15): collectibility threshold, shipping/handling election, IP licensing.
  – Leases (ASC 842 vs. IFRS 16): dual lessee P&L model vs. single front-loaded model; sale-leaseback gain.
  – Financial Instruments & Credit Losses (ASC 320/321/326 vs. IFRS 9): Day-1 lifetime CECL vs. 3-stage ECL; no equity FVOCI.
  – Non-Financial Assets (ASC 330/350/360/730 vs. IAS 2/16/36/38): LIFO, no impairment reversals, R&D expensing, 2-step undiscounted PP&E impairment.
  – Consolidation & Liabilities/Equity (ASC 810/480/470 vs. IFRS 10/IAS 32): VIE/VOE model, mezzanine equity, single-liability convertible debt.
